title: Stable persistence with independent Audit ownership
question: Which schema changes are required to redistribute modules safely?
context: Architecture decision recorded by the agent under the owner's explicit design delegation. Phase tasks and implementation remain deferred.
decision: Preserve schema-2 authority columns, table names, identity codecs and populated rows. Core owns six authority tables; Audit owns the existing audit table, migration/adoption, health, insertion and retention. Fresh core-only installs omit Audit; existing audit tables are fully checked and adopted without row rewriting or destructive adoption rollback.
rationale: Scopes, tenant resolution, DevTools and Filament need no additional AzGuard table. Current StorageSchema and delegate migrations create/drop Audit together with authority storage, so ownership must change deliberately before 1.0 while names/history and same-transaction guarantees remain stable.

evidence.note: The owner delegated architecture choices and required an affirmative target design.
